note: Price Watch tracks completed auction results, not live listings. Every record below was certified at ingest against a published source naming the car, the price, the house, and the date; the source is linked on each record. Wave 4 certified 7 results (2026-10-13); wave 5 added 4 more to the same standard; wave 7 (stage 2) added 8 more; wave 8 (stage 3) added 9 more; wave 9 (stage 4) added 9 more; wave 10 (stage 5) added 9 more; wave 11 (stage 6) added 10 more, 56 certified results in all. Stage 5 gave every record a chassis key (populated where the source names the chassis, null otherwise) and condition and mileage fields (populated only where a source states them, null otherwise, never inferred); stage 6 populated those fields from its sources wherever they stated them, linked eight of its ten new records to model pages the atlas already carried, and added the Buy page's first cohort rung: per-model result ranges computed only from certified records in a single currency, with the count shown. Stage 6 extends the certified-results set only: the listings ingest described in earlier roadmaps is not built, and no listing, estimate or unsold lot appears here. Prices are historical facts about one specific car on one specific day, not asking prices, not estimates, and not a valuation of any other example. Rotation 25 (stage 7) added 10 more to the same standard, 66 certified results in all: six further F40 sales in euros took the F40/EUR cohort to eight certified results, the first cohort at the T-CARS-1 trigger, so stage 7 also ships the cohort machinery: cohort medians for cohorts of eight or more, computed in the build from certified records only and published in data/v1/cohorts.json, n shown wherever a figure prints. Stage 7 also certified the 2021 Gooding sale of Miura chassis 3378, the first chassis to appear twice in the certified set (T-CARS-4). Results that could not be certified to that standard were skipped, not estimated (see skippedSources). Rotation 26 (stage 8) added 17 more to the same standard, 83 certified results in all: the pass re-broadened the four cohorts that stood at two: Corvette (five more sales, to seven in dollars), Ford GT (six more, to eight in dollars, the second cohort at the T-CARS-1 trigger, printing its build-computed median beside the F40's), Duesenberg Model J (three more, to five in dollars) and Aston Martin DB5 (three more: one each in dollars, euros and pounds, taking the dollar cohort to three and the euro cohort to two). Every new record links to a model record the atlas already carried; the orphan count is unmoved at 27. Two candidates were skipped and recorded (see skippedSources): a GT40 whose sources disagree on the sale day, and a GT40 whose sources disagree on the final price. Rotation 27 (stage 9) added 13 more to the same standard, 96 certified results in all: the pass worked the near-threshold cohorts: Corvette (three more sales, to ten in dollars, the third cohort at the T-CARS-1 trigger), Duesenberg Model J (four more, to nine in dollars, the fourth cohort at the trigger), Aston Martin DB5 (three more: two in dollars, to five, and one in euros, to three) and Lamborghini Miura (three more: two in dollars, to five, and one in euros, to three). Every new record links to a model record the atlas already carried; the orphan count is unmoved at 27. Three candidates were skipped and recorded (see skippedSources): three 1967 Corvette L88 sales whose sources disagree on the final price, on the Artcurial F40 precedent. Rotation 28 (stage 10) added 11 more to the same standard, 107 certified results in all: the pass worked the two cohorts that stood at five and the euro Miura cohort that stood at three: Aston Martin DB5 (three more in dollars, to eight, the fifth cohort at the T-CARS-1 trigger), Lamborghini Miura (three more in dollars, to eight, the sixth cohort at the trigger, and five more in euros, to eight, the seventh cohort at the trigger). Every new record links to a model record the atlas already carried; the orphan count is unmoved at 27. Three candidates were skipped and recorded (see skippedSources): a Miura SV whose sources disagree on the sale day, a Miura S whose sources disagree on the currency of the result, and a DB5 held to the pass's own corroboration standard. Rotation 29 (stage 11) added 12 more to the same standard, 119 certified results in all: the pass worked the two cohorts that stood nearest the trigger below eight: Ferrari F40 (six more in dollars, to eight, the eighth cohort at the T-CARS-1 trigger) and Aston Martin DB5 (five more in euros, to eight, the ninth cohort at the trigger, and one more in dollars, to nine). The DB5 in dollars is chassis DB5/1990/L, held at stage 10 to the pass's own corroboration standard and certified here only because a second source agreeing on the figure was found in this pass (see the record's source line). One F40 chassis (ZFFMN34A0L0086620) appears twice in this pass alone, sold at Amelia in March 2025 and again at Pebble Beach in August 2025. Every new record links to a model record the atlas already carried; the orphan count is unmoved at 27. Two candidates were skipped and recorded (see skippedSources): two DB5 sales in euros whose sources date the sale only to a two-day event, not to the day (the SSJ precedent). Rotation 30 (stage 12) added 6 more to the same standard, 125 certified results in all, all six McLaren F1 sales in dollars: chassis 014 at RM Auctions Monterey in 2006 ($1,705,000), chassis 062 at Gooding & Company Pebble Beach in 2010 ($3,575,000), chassis 066 at Gooding & Company Pebble Beach in 2013 ($8,470,000), chassis 073, the LM-Specification car, at RM Sotheby's Monterey in 2015 ($13,750,000), chassis 044 at Bonhams Quail Lodge in 2017 ($15,620,000), and the F1 GTR chassis 10R at RM Sotheby's Monterey in 2026 ($34,655,000). The F1 GTR is carried on the F1 model record on the precedent of the F40 LM's record on the F40 record: a factory variant of the model, named as the variant on the record itself. With the two standing results the F1 dollar cohort reaches eight certified sales, the T-CARS-1 trigger, so stage 12 also fires the cohort machinery a tenth time and every cohort at n≥2 is now a benchmark cohort. Five further candidates were skipped and recorded (see skippedSources): three whose sources disagree on the figure or its basis, one sealed sale whose result was never published, and one whose house-published currency could not be established. Every new record links to a model record the atlas already carried; the orphan count is unmoved at 27. Rotation 31 (stage 13) added 5 more to the same standard, 130 certified results in all, all five Toyota 2000GT sales in dollars, working the certified set's breadth from its smallest linked cohort: chassis MF1010088 at Gooding & Company Pebble Beach in 2014 ($1,155,000), an unnumbered-chassis car at RM Auctions' Don Davis Collection in 2013 ($1,155,000), chassis MF1010100 at RM Sotheby's Elkhart Collection in 2020 ($912,500), chassis MF10L10111 at RM Sotheby's Arizona in 2018 ($665,000), and chassis MF1010158 at RM Sotheby's Petersen Automotive Museum Auction in 2018 ($511,000). With the standing Toyota-Shelby result the 2000GT dollar cohort reaches six certified sales: a new range cohort, below the T-CARS-1 trigger, so no new benchmark fires and the ten benchmark cohorts stand unchanged. Three further candidates were skipped and recorded (see skippedSources): one whose result figure was never published, one the sources disagree on whether it sold, and one dated only to a two-day event. Every new record links to a model record the atlas already carried; the orphan count is unmoved at 27. Rotation 32 (stage 14) added 3 more to the same standard, 133 certified results in all, all three Toyota 2000GT sales in dollars, working the one range cohort stage 13 opened: chassis MF10-10101 at Bring a Trailer in 2021 ($850,000, 19,339 km), chassis MF1010088 at RM Sotheby's Amelia Island in 2016 ($797,500, the same car's second certified sale, after its 2014 Gooding & Company result), and an unnumbered-chassis car at RM Sotheby's Amelia Island in 2015 ($880,000). The 2000GT dollar cohort reaches nine certified sales and passes the T-CARS-1 trigger: it publishes its median as the programme's eleventh benchmark cohort, and no range-only cohort remains. Each of the three records was certified against two independent sources agreeing on car, house, sale day and price. Three further candidates were skipped and recorded (see skippedSources): one whose direct record read failed and lacked a second source stating price and day together, one confirmed by a single index only, and four dated only to multi-day events. Every new record links to a model record the atlas already carried; the orphan count is unmoved at 27. Rotation 33 (stage 15) added 3 more to the same standard, 136 certified results in all, all three Mercedes-Benz 300 SL Gullwing sales in dollars at RM Sotheby's Amelia Island, working the certified set's breadth from its single-record model pages: chassis 198.040.5500693 in 2022 ($2,040,000), chassis 198.040.6500292 in 2018 ($1,077,500) and chassis 198.040.4500116 in 2017 ($1,358,500). With the standing Alloy Gullwing record the 300 SL dollar cohort reaches four certified sales: a new cohort at n>=2, below the T-CARS-1 trigger, so the eleven benchmark cohorts stand unchanged and one range cohort stands again. Each of the three records was certified against two independent sources agreeing on car, house, sale day and price. Two further candidates were skipped and recorded (see skippedSources): a 2025 Arizona Gullwing whose sources attribute it to different chassis, and the carried 2000GT candidate MF1010219, for which this pass's fresh search again found no second source stating price and sale day together. Every new record links to a model record the atlas already carried; the orphan count is unmoved at 27. Rotation 34 (stage 16) added 4 more to the same standard, 140 certified results in all, all four Mercedes-Benz 300 SL Gullwing sales in dollars, deepening the cohort stage 15 opened: chassis 198.040.5500031 at Gooding & Company Amelia Island in 2023 ($1,737,500), chassis 198.040.5500243 at RM Sotheby's Arizona in 2022 ($1,710,000), chassis 198.040.6500146 at Bonhams' Quail Auction in 2022 ($1,737,500) and chassis 198.040.5500800 at RM Sotheby's Monterey in 2018 ($1,435,000). The 300 SL dollar cohort reaches eight certified sales, past the T-CARS-1 priced trigger, so the build now publishes its benchmark median ($1,723,750) alongside the eleven standing benchmarks. Each of the four records was certified against two independent sources agreeing on car, house, sale day and price. Two candidates were skipped and recorded (see skippedSources): the carried 2000GT candidate MF1010219, for which this pass's fresh search again found no independent second source stating price and sale day together, and the 2025 Arizona Gullwing whose sources still attribute it to different chassis. Every new record links to the SL model record the atlas already carried; the orphan count is unmoved at 27. Rotation 35 (stage 17) added 3 more to the same standard, 143 certified results in all: a 1991 Ferrari F40 (chassis ZFFMN34A6M0087627) at RM Sotheby's SHIFT/Monterey in 2020 ($1,386,000), a 1969 Lamborghini Miura P400 S (chassis 3874) at RM Sotheby's Elkhart Collection in 2020 ($1,160,000) and a 1955 Mercedes-Benz 300 SL Gullwing (chassis 198.040.5500533) at the same Elkhart sale ($1,495,500), deepening the F40, Miura and 300 SL dollar cohorts from eight certified sales to nine each. Each record was certified against two independent sources agreeing on car, house, sale day and price. Four candidates were skipped and recorded (see skippedSources): the carried 2000GT candidate MF1010219, for which this pass's fresh search again found no independent second source stating price and sale day together; the contested-chassis 2025 Arizona Gullwing; and two Broad Arrow 2000GT sales (Monterey Jet Center 2022 and Radius 2023) whose sources disagree on the final price. Every new record links to a model record the atlas already carried; the orphan count is unmoved at 27. Rotation 36 (stage 18) added 3 more to the same standard, 146 certified results in all: a 1955 Mercedes-Benz 300 SL Gullwing (chassis 198.040.5500289) at RM Sotheby's Monterey in 2023 ($1,737,500), a 1955 Mercedes-Benz 300 SL Gullwing (chassis 198.040.5500666) at Gooding & Company Amelia Island in 2024 ($1,765,000) and a 1972 Lamborghini Miura P400 SV (chassis 5048) at Broad Arrow Auctions' Monterey Jet Center sale in 2024 ($2,700,000), deepening the 300 SL dollar cohort from nine certified sales to eleven and the Miura dollar cohort from nine to ten. Each record was certified against two independent sources agreeing on car, house, sale day and price. Six candidates were skipped and recorded (see skippedSources): the carried 2000GT candidate MF1010219, for which this pass's fresh search again found no independent second source stating price and sale day together; the contested-chassis 2025 Arizona Gullwing; the two Broad Arrow 2000GT sales whose sources still disagree on the final price; a Ferrari F40 'Minty Forty' whose sources disagree on the final price; and a Ferrari F40 whose sources disagree on the sale day. Every new record links to a model record the atlas already carried; the orphan count is unmoved at 27.
